title: Ericsson Q3 Earnings Beat Expectations, Announces Price Hikes as AI Drives Up Component Costs
key_facts: Ericsson's third-quarter revenue was SEK 59.5 billion (about $6.0 billion), up 6% on the year and above the $5.79 billion expected.
Adjusted EBITA was SEK 10.1 billion, against about SEK 7.93 billion expected; shares rose as much as 11%, the biggest one-day gain since January.
New chief executive Per Narvinger said the AI boom is raising equipment manufacturing costs and Ericsson cannot absorb them indefinitely.
Ericsson has raised prices in new bids and is negotiating higher prices with existing customers, but long-term contracts may delay the effect and could pressure gross margins through 2027.
He warned that telecom operators may pass higher costs on to consumers; some customers have brought orders forward.
Adjusted gross margin was 47.7%, against 48.1% a year earlier.
Ericsson will merge two Asian business units and restructure its Enterprise Wireless business.
quote_evidence: Swedish telecom equipment maker Ericsson (ERIC.US) reported third-quarter results on Thursday, with both profit and revenue beating market expectations on strong demand for mobile network equipment in core markets, sending its Stockholm-listed shares up as much as 11% intraday — the biggest single-day gain since January this year.
He further warned that telecom operators may ultimately pass these higher costs on to end consumers.
why_it_matters_hint: AI demand for components is raising the price of mobile network equipment.
